incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: multiple 401s observed for auth-service across prod-us-east-1 and prod-eu-west-1. Spike started ~2026-03-15T09:20Z — alert threshold breached. Investigate and triage.
Maria Nguyen: I'm on it. seeing ~1200 401/min on auth-service-01 and 02. customers hitting session refresh failures.
Kevin Chen: any signs of config push or deploy in the window? I don't see any deploys in the last hour.
Tess Ramirez: rolling logs for auth-proxy show repeated token validations from a small set of IPs, looks like a replay/credential stuffing pattern. sample:```[2026-03-15T09:21:12Z] auth-proxy validate_token user_id=acct-982 status=401 src_ip=45.33.21.7 token="Bearer sk-***REDACTED***"```
Maria Nguyen: hmm thanks. also seeing debug-log-forwarder delivering debug logs to third-party indexer; some tokens might be present in those debug payloads. not confirmed yet.
Arjun Patel: if logs leaked full headers, we need immediate key/secret rotation and revoke refresh tokens. Impact assessment first: I see 4 paying customers with elevated failed sessions, ~20 non-prod customers hit but not critical.
Security Bot: flagged suspicious IPs: 45.33.21.0/24, 198.51.100.14, 203.0.113.42. Recommend block and trace egress.
Kevin Chen: I'm going to spin up an auth-proxy fallback with stricter header redaction and drop debug-forwarder. will post commands.
Kevin Chen: runbook commands: ```# block CIDR on WAF
aws wafv2 update-ip-set --name suspicious-ips --scope REGIONAL --addresses 45.33.21.0/24 198.51.100.14/32 203.0.113.42/32```
Kevin Chen: ```# disable debug-forwarder service
kubectl -n infra scale deployment debug-forwarder --replicas=0```
Tess Ramirez: taking ownership of customer comms draft. Maria, can you confirm which customer tokens were present in logs so we can include rotation guidance?
Maria Nguyen: confirmed two customer sessions show redacted token patterns in forwarded logs; will pull full file and send secure link. prepping list now.
Arjun Patel: immediate mitigations: 1) block suspicious IP ranges 2) scale to fallback proxy (Kevin) 3) rotate internal service account keys for debug-forwarder and auth-proxy 4) trigger global refresh token invalidation for affected tenant IDs 5) notify CS for customer outreach.
Tess Ramirez: drafting email templates. Proposed severity P1 with affected customer list + mitigating steps + CTA to rotate app secrets.
Security Bot: recommended key rotation commands: ```# rotate debug-forwarder SA key (GCP example)
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create new-key.json --iam-account=debug-forwarder@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# then delete old key by id
gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete OLD_KEY_ID --iam-account=debug-forwarder@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com```
Maria Nguyen: I'm revoking refresh tokens for tenant IDs: tenant_44, tenant_71 now. running script: `./tools/invalidate_refresh_tokens --tenants tenant_44,tenant_71 --reason "suspected-token-exposure"`
Kevin Chen: fallback proxy up with header redaction rules and stricter rate limits. testing: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer test" https://auth-fallback.prod.redwood.com/health` -> 200.
Tess Ramirez: CS/AM notified for tenant_44 and tenant_71, initial outreach scheduled in 20m. advising immediate re-login and secret rotation steps.
Arjun Patel: Customer impact: tenant_44 reported failed background synces for 18 users; no data exfil reports so far. risk: medium-high until rotation confirmed.
Maria Nguyen: found evidence that one debug-forwarder batch included full Authorization headers for ~12 requests. grabbing exact lines and will upload to secure incident artifact store.
Kevin Chen: rotating debug-forwarder SA keys now, will rotate auth-proxy keys after. ETA 8m.
Security Bot: note: please treat artifacts as high-sensitivity. add tag "incident-3098765432" to artifacts.
Tess Ramirez: added incident channel to the CS ticket and internal status page. publishing initial incident note (P1, auth tokens exposed in forwarded debug logs) in 10m.
Maria Nguyen: post-rotation checks: watch for token replay attempts and 401 rates dropping. also schedule scheduled key rotation for the forwarder in vault.
Arjun Patel: next steps: 1) finish rotations 2) confirm no additional forwarders leaked headers 3) run forensic on egress to external indexer 4) prepare postmortem timeline. who will lead the postmortem?
Kevin Chen: I can own postmortem since I touched the proxy changes.
Maria Nguyen: I'll collect logs and create timeline. Tess will draft customer comms. Arjun will lead root-cause analysis.
incident-bot: Update: mitigations applied: CIDR blocked, debug-forwarder scaled to 0, SA keys rotated, refresh tokens invalidated for affected tenants. Continue monitoring.
Tess Ramirez: posting summary for execs in #incidents-summary in 30m. adding recommended action: remove header dumps from debug-forwarder payloads permanently and enforce redaction at ingestion boundary. :lock:
Maria Nguyen: monitoring shows 401 rate down to baseline after rotations and blocks. still watching for other IPs.
Arjun Patel: high-level customer impact note for postmortem: exposure limited to forwarded debug batch; affected tenants required re-login and secret rotation; no confirmed exfil of customer PII.
Kevin Chen: closing immediate mitigation tasks, leaving this thread open for postmortem artifacts and timeline updates.
Tess Ramirez: thanks everyone — great triage. will schedule postmortem meeting for 09:00 UTC tomorrow. :thumbsup:
